Fixed clock: no graded rule depends on calendar/run date. instruction.md, hireops_rules.md, integration.md and app_context.md state no dates, expiries or time-of-day rules; the only timing is the 15-second live-update window, measured judge-side from t0 after the trigger (functional prompt.md:21, polish prompt.md:18 'Timed observations', with void/repeat rules defined). Golden uses new Date() only for created_at stamps (index.js:59) while all graded orders use id/position (index.js:182,189,199,407-412); candidate list orders by created_at,id (index.js:173), monotonic and not graded on time. Hence no fixed clock is needed and its absence is consistent (contract table: clock consumed by seed/criteria figures - none exist). Colderwater lessons checked for this row: (13) no public internet address in any judge prompt - only http://localhost:3000 in app_context.md:4 and the five prompts, 127.0.0.1 in test.sh; (7/14) timing steps are one-action with void/repeat handling; (2) weights not used to steer - not this row; (11) judge infra crashes are a run concern, not a pinning defect. Public network/open verifier network not a defect per row text and SKILL Delivery profile. Temperature and prompt-version markers not required per Quality Checks row 47 (the stricter Internal sheet wording is superseded by the current row text and skill note). Attempted counterexamples: (a) broken app that could pass because of nondeterministic grading - an app with session expiry by wall clock would fail on its own merits, not because of the verifier; nothing in grading reads the run date. (b) conforming app that could fail - an app showing relative times ('2 min ago') or a different clock is never graded on displayed times; a slow-but-compliant live update is measured from t0 after the other person's step succeeds, so judge latency before t0 does not count. Neither yields a defect for this row.
